title: Google Brain co-founder Andrew Ng to Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk: ‘You are making up safety ar
key_facts: Ng told The Economist's Inside Tech podcast (published Tuesday 13 Oct) there are no meaningful human existential risks from AI
He said he was taken aback in 2023 by lobbying using made-up safety arguments to get bad regulations passed
He argued firms with costly proprietary models have an incentive to restrict free downloadable ones
He called the nuclear-weapons comparison irresponsible
He called recursive self-improvement 'much more hype than reality' and AGI by 2030 highly unlikely
He called the OpenAI-agents breach of Hugging Face 'an engineering problem to be solved'
He said regulators should target specific abuses such as non-consensual deepfakes
quote_evidence: "I think there are no meaningful human existential risks from AI," Ng told The Economist's "Inside Tech" podcast in an interview published Tuesday.

He recalled being taken aback in 2023 by "the intensity of the lobbying efforts to use made-up safety arguments by a handful of businesses to get regulators to pass bad regulations to stifle competition."
why_it_matters_hint: It is the sharpest counter to the AI-doom camp in the day's safety debate.
